question: Under the Indian Contract Act, is compensation for breach of contract payable for remote and indirect loss?

gold.quote: Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sus tained by reason

reference_answer: No. Section 73 excludes compensation for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach.

question: Which agreements are contracts under the Indian Contract Act?

gold.quote: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free

reference_answer: Section 10: agreements made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and not expressly declared void.

question: Who is competent to contract?

gold.quote: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of

reference_answer: Section 11: a person of the age of majority under the law to which he is subject, of sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting by any law.

question: What is the status of an agreement to do an act impossible in itself?

gold.quote: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void.

reference_answer: Section 56: such an agreement is void.

question: When is consent said to be free under the Indian Contract Act?

gold.quote: Consent is said to be free when it is not caused by

reference_answer: Section 14: when it is not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake.

question: If a contract names a sum payable on breach, how much compensation can the injured party recover?

gold.quote: has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may

reference_answer: Section 74: reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved.

question: Can a court limit anticipatory bail so that it expires when the charge-sheet is filed?

gold.quote: expiry clauses inserted at inception are unsustainable
should not invariably be limited to a fixed period; it

reference_answer: Ordinarily no: anticipatory bail continues without fixed expiry and expiry clauses inserted at inception are unsustainable (Sushila Aggarwal; Sumit v. State of U.P.).

question: Does the filing of a charge-sheet bar the grant of anticipatory bail according to Bharat Chaudhary?

gold.quote: reported in (2003)8 SCC 77, this Court held that there is no

reference_answer: No. Bharat Chaudhary v. State of Bihar, (2003) 8 SCC 77, held there is no restriction in Section 438 CrPC on granting anticipatory bail even after a charge-sheet is filed and cognizance taken.

question: What can an accused already on bail do when new cognizable and non-bailable offences are added to the charge-sheet?

gold.quote: The accused can surrender and apply for bail for newly

reference_answer: The accused can surrender and apply for bail for the newly added offences; if bail is refused he can be arrested.
